data.scenario_text: A <m>18</m>-foot ladder leans against a wall, with its foot <m>5</m> feet from the base of the wall.
data.find_task: Find the angle the ladder makes with the ground. Do not round until the final answer; then round to two decimal places as necessary.
data.solution_steps:
Part (a). A correct sketch shows a right triangle with the right angle marked and only the two given lengths written in: the leg adjacent to \theta is 5\text{ ft} and the hypotenuse is 18\text{ ft}. The third side is not given, so it stays unlabeled, and the angle should not be filled in.

Part (b). Both given quantities are lengths and the unknown is an angle, so the answer comes from an inverse function. In the triangle the given sides are the leg adjacent to \theta and the hypotenuse; the ratio built from exactly those two sides is cosine, \cos\theta=\dfrac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}, so we solve \cos\theta=\dfrac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}} for \theta using the inverse cosine.

Substituting and computing, \theta=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{18}\right).

This gives \theta \approx 73.87^\circ, so the angle the ladder makes with the ground is \boxed{73.87^\circ}.

Part (a). A correct sketch shows a right triangle with the right angle marked and only the two given lengths written in: the leg adjacent to \theta is 6\text{ ft} and the hypotenuse is 22\text{ ft}. The third side is not given, so it stays unlabeled, and the angle should not be filled in.

Part (b). Both given quantities are lengths and the unknown is an angle, so the answer comes from an inverse function. In the triangle the given sides are the leg adjacent to \theta and the hypotenuse; the ratio built from exactly those two sides is cosine, \cos\theta=\dfrac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}, so we solve \cos\theta=\dfrac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}} for \theta using the inverse cosine.

Substituting and computing, \theta=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{6}{22}\right).

This gives \theta \approx 74.17^\circ, so the angle the ladder makes with the ground is \boxed{74.17^\circ}.
